description.text: The Diocese of Würzburg was founded in 741 by Saint Boniface, who consecrated Saint Burchard as its first bishop. Burchard built the first cathedral and buried St. Kilian there, establishing a strong ecclesiastical presence in the region.

In 752 or 753 the bishopric was granted immunity for all its possessions, giving the bishops secular jurisdiction and laying the groundwork for the later Prince-Bishopric. The diocese survived as a Latin Church diocese to the present day, having lost all temporal power after the Napoleonic wars.

curiosities.text: The first mention of Würzburg appears in 704 as Castellum Virtebuch.
Saint Kilian, an Irish missionary, converted the Frankish duke Gozbert, leading to the construction of the first church at Marienberg.
Burchard’s cathedral was the burial site of St. Kilian and his companions, cementing the diocese’s spiritual significance.
Bishop Arno rebuilt the cathedral between 855 and 892 after it was destroyed by lightning.
The bishopric’s temporal authority ended with the secularization of the Prince-Bishopric during the Napoleonic wars.
